Q710.L1t: The minute hand of a clock turns 360 degrees every hour, while the hour hand turns 30 degrees every hour.
Q710.L2t: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute and the hour hand moves 0.5 degrees per minute, so the minute hand gains 5.5 degrees per minute on the hour hand.
Q710.L3t: Between 6 and 7 the angle between the hands is |180 - 5.5t| for t minutes past 6, so 110 degrees occurs at two times, t = 70/5.5 and t = 290/5.5, and the time away is the difference between them.
Q710.L4t: John was away for exactly 40 minutes.
Q710.L2f: On a standard clock the hour hand moves 1 degree per minute, and the minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute.
Q710.L3f: The two times when the hands are 110 degrees apart after 6 are about 13.4 minutes and 51.4 minutes past the hour, which are separated by 38 minutes.

Q649.L1t: Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through an opening or around an obstacle, and it is strongest when the opening is comparable to the wavelength.
Q649.L2t: For a single slit of width a, dark minima occur at angles where a sin(theta) = m times the wavelength, with m = 1, 2, 3, and so on.
Q649.L3t: The first minimum at 45 degrees requires wavelength = 0.14 m times sin 45 degrees, which is about 0.099 m, and frequency equals the 350 m/s speed divided by that wavelength.
Q649.L4t: The first minimum at that angle falls at about 3,500 Hz.
Q649.L2f: Diffraction through a slit is negligible for sound, because audible wavelengths are always much smaller than a slit of this size.
Q649.L3f: The wavelength that produces the first minimum at 45 degrees works out to about 0.7 m, and dividing the 350 m/s speed by it gives the frequency.
Q649.L4f: The sound first disappears at the lowest frequency listed, about one-seventh of the highest frequency listed.

Q327.L1t: A cube has six faces, eight vertices, and twelve edges, and each vertex touches exactly three faces.
Q327.L2t: The number 1001 factors into the primes 7, 11, and 13.
Q327.L3t: Summing the eight vertex products gives (a+b)(c+d)(e+f), where each bracket is the sum of one pair of opposite faces, so 1001 must split into three integer factors each at least 2.
Q327.L4t: The three opposite-face sums are 7, 11, and 13, so the face numbers add up to 31.
Q327.L2f: Each face of the cube touches exactly four vertices, so each face number appears in four of the eight vertex products.
Q327.L3f: The total of the vertex products equals the sum of the faces multiplied together, so only the two smallest prime factors of 1001 matter and the face sum is 7 + 11.
Q327.L4f: The sum of the numbers on the faces is 18.
